Downwind exposure: places downwind of sources of pollution

Source: R/dwn.R
dwnexp.Rd

Whether each place lies downwind of sources of pollution in each period, and how far off the wind's line it lies: the instruments of the papers that let the wind carry smoke from fires that move from day to day (Bao and Da 2026) or from a fixed set of sources (Ayesh 2023), for the instrumental-variable estimators ivfe(), ppmlcf() and expgmm().

Usage

dwnexp(
  sx,
  sy,
  sper,
  sdir,
  rx,
  ry,
  rid = NULL,
  rule = "sector",
  half = 30,
  rad = Inf,
  from = TRUE,
  lonlat = FALSE,
  wrap = TRUE,
  dwt = "mult"
)

Arguments

sx, sy

The coordinates of the sources.

sper

NULL (one period) or the period of each source (labels).

sdir

The wind direction at each source, degrees clockwise from north.

rx, ry

The coordinates of the places: points, or the vertices of their polygons for rule = "wedge".

rid

NULL (each row a place) or the place of each row of rx (labels); for rule = "wedge", the vertices of a place in order.

rule

"sector", "wedge" or "angle".

half

The half-angle of the sector, degrees from 0 to 180.

rad

The radius of the sector: a positive number or Inf.

from

TRUE when sdir is where the wind blows from.

lonlat

TRUE for longitude and latitude in degrees.

wrap

TRUE for the angle about the circle (rule = "angle").

dwt

"mult", "div" or "none": the distance weight of the angle (rule = "angle").

Value

A data frame, one row per place and period (places fastest): id, per, and n and any for "sector" and "wedge", or angle, dist and z for "angle" (NA where a period has no source at a distance).

Details

The sources are rows (sx, sy) with a period each (sper: a day, a plume-day's date, a year) and the wind there (sdir, degrees clockwise from north, where the wind blows from with from = TRUE: sdir + 180 is then the direction it blows to). The places are points (rx, ry) or, for rule = "wedge", polygons whose vertices are the rows of each rid in order. Three rules:

  • "sector": a place is downwind of a source when the bearing from the source to the place is within half degrees of the direction the wind blows to, and the place within rad of the source (a place at the source counts). This is the point ("centroid") instrument of Bao and Da (2026, sec. 3.3), each county collapsed to one point and "the great-circle bearing from the plume anchor to that point" within 30 degrees either side of the mean wind to-direction (half = 30, rad = Inf).

  • "wedge": a place's polygon meets the wedge of half-angle half and radius rad about that direction from the source: their baseline instrument, "a wedge-shaped transport corridor" with a half-angle of 30 degrees and a radius of 1,000 km, a county downwind "if its census polygon intersects this wedge" (sec. 3.3). Planar coordinates only (projected, rad in their unit). The polygon meets the wedge when a vertex lies in it, the apex lies in the polygon, or an edge crosses a side or the arc.

  • "angle": per period, the angle between the bearing from the mean point of the sources to the place and the direction of their mean wind vector, and the mean distance from the place to the sources (those at its own location left out): Ayesh's (2023, sec. 4) instrument, "the absolute value of lat_j - DirT_t" with DirT_t the "average annual wind direction ... from the twelve rice growing districts", weighted by "the mean distance from the rice growing districts" (for a source district "the mean distance from eleven other rice growing districts", n. 23).

For "sector" and "wedge", n counts the period's sources that reach the place and any is 1 when one does; Bao and Da's instrument is the sum of any over the days of a county-month (their eq 1), which stats::aggregate() gives (see the examples). With several plumes a day, give each its own row with that day's period.

The choices the papers leave open, as arguments:

  • from: Bao and Da convert the "from-direction" to a "to-direction" by adding 180 degrees; Ayesh subtracts the wind direction from the azimuth without saying which way the direction is recorded. from = TRUE (the default) adds 180 degrees, so that the angle is 0 for a place straight downwind; from = FALSE uses sdir as given.

  • wrap: the angle about the circle, at most 180 (the default), or the plain absolute difference of the two bearings in [0, 360), Ayesh's formula as written.

  • dwt: Ayesh does not say how the mean distance weights the angle: "mult" (the default) gives z = angle * dist, "div" angle / dist, "none" the angle alone.

  • lonlat: with TRUE, x and y are longitude and latitude in degrees, bearings are initial great-circle bearings and distances kilometres (haversine, radius 6371.0088 km); else planar, distances in the coordinates' unit.

The direction of the wind at a source is the user's: Bao and Da take the speed-weighted circular mean of the to-direction over the wind grid cells inside each plume (windiv() averages directions the same way), and keep only plumes of medium and heavy density (smkiv() reads those classes). As instruments these are valid only if the wind carries the outcome nowhere but through the exposure.

References

Bao, J. and Da, Y. (2026). Wildfire smoke and crime: evidence from California. Working paper, Renmin University of China.

Ayesh, A. (2023). Burned agricultural biomass, air pollution and crime. Journal of Environmental Economics and Management, 122, 102887. doi:10.1016/j.jeem.2023.102887

See also

windiv(), smkiv(), updwn(), ivfe()

Examples

# two plumes on day 1, one on day 2; four county points (planar, km)
s <- data.frame(x = c(0, 50, 0), y = c(0, 0, 0), day = c(1, 1, 2),
                from = c(180, 270, 0))
p <- data.frame(x = c(0, 100, 0, -80), y = c(100, 10, -60, 0))
r <- dwnexp(s$x, s$y, s$day, s$from, p$x, p$y)
r
#>   id per n any
#> 1  1   1 1   1
#> 2  2   1 1   1
#> 3  3   1 0   0
#> 4  4   1 0   0
#> 5  1   2 0   0
#> 6  2   2 0   0
#> 7  3   2 1   1
#> 8  4   2 0   0
# the county-month count of downwind days (Bao and Da 2026, eq 1)
r$month <- 1
aggregate(any ~ id + month, r, sum)
#>   id month any
#> 1  1     1   1
#> 2  2     1   1
#> 3  3     1   1
#> 4  4     1   0

# Ayesh's instrument: the angle off the mean wind of the source
# districts, times the mean distance to them
dwnexp(c(0, 10), c(0, 0), c(2020, 2020), c(240, 250), c(30, -30, 5),
       c(20, -20, 0), rule = "angle")
#>   id  per     angle     dist         z
#> 1  1 2020  13.65981 32.16989  439.4346
#> 2  2 2020 175.25512 40.38844 7078.2802
#> 3  3 2020  65.00000  5.00000  325.0000

# the wedge against a square county
sq <- data.frame(id = 1, x = c(-10, 10, 10, -10), y = c(40, 40, 60, 60))
dwnexp(0, 0, NULL, 180, sq$x, sq$y, sq$id, rule = "wedge", rad = 100)
#>   id per n any
#> 1  1   1 1   1
